title: Which frustration graphs give free fermions?
shortTitle: When interacting spins have a free spectrum
oneLine: A graph criterion characterises whole-spectrum freeness at every coupling under faithful Pauli realisation; exact sector certificates reveal a larger, carefully distinguished class.
abstract: This unrefereed mathematical-physics candidate proves a converse to the even-hole, claw-free theorem for faithful Pauli realisations. Outside that graph class, whole-spectrum free couplings form a proper algebraic exceptional set. It also gives exact four-block formulas for periodic Fendley chains of lengths eight and nine, a central-coefficient certification criterion, and heredity of a weaker prescribed-mode property. A revised trace-projector argument proves parity-pattern completeness for a three-mode subclass. Exact checks cover 107 graphs; another 1,621 examples remain numerical candidates. The work does not provide a general sector classification or new fermionic ladder operators.
narration: An interacting quantum system can have an unexpectedly simple pattern of energies. Instead of solving for every energy separately, sometimes we can obtain them by adding and subtracting a short list of basic energies. This is called a free-fermion spectrum. A graph records which terms in the spin Hamiltonian anticommute. Earlier work showed that excluding two kinds of induced subgraph, a claw and an even cycle, guarantees a free spectrum. This research candidate proves the converse under an important assumption: the Pauli terms must faithfully represent the graph algebra, and their couplings can vary independently. Under those conditions, the graph criterion is exact. Outside the class, couplings giving a free whole spectrum lie on an algebraic exceptional set. That does not rule out specially constrained physical models. The whole spectrum is only part of the story. A system can split into invariant blocks, each with a free spectrum. The paper gives explicit four-block formulas for periodic chains of eight and nine spins, valid at every coupling. At special couplings some blocks merge into larger coefficient sectors, and those sectors need not themselves be free. The evidence package contains written proofs, exact identities for one hundred and seven graphs, and numerical checks of a larger catalogue. A review exposed a missing counting argument. The revision repairs it by proving that every allowed parity pattern actually occurs in the stated three-mode class. More than sixteen hundred other examples remain numerical candidates. This is not a general solution for every spin chain. This is Evidence Press, Which frustration graphs give free fermions, released on the twenty-seventh of September twenty twenty-six, version one point zero candidate. It is unrefereed. The paper and evidence package are linked on this page. This AI-generated synthetic voice adds no scientific evidence.
keyResults: Faithful Pauli whole-spectrum freeness for every independent real coupling is equivalent to the graph being even-hole- and claw-free.
Outside that class, whole-spectrum free couplings form a proper real algebraic exceptional set.
Four explicit invariant free blocks at all couplings for periodic Fendley lengths 8 and 9; merged coefficient sectors need not be free at exceptional couplings.
Weak prescribed-mode heredity and a three-mode parity-completeness proposition; strict Z-heredity remains open.
107 exact graph certificates; 1,621 further sampled-coupling candidates are not exact classifications.
evidence: Written mathematical arguments, two exact implementations, 107 graph identities spanning 792 coefficient-label classes and 1,404 central characters, numerical replays and rejection controls, physical-spin checks, source comparisons and a point-by-point review response.
statusDetail: Unrefereed candidate with producer-coordinated model review and local checks. The separately implemented exact checker passed all 107 graphs. The slower original FLINT route was partially replayed, not completed. Numerical rechecks cover 1,728 positives, 1,201 negatives and 64 additional samples. No formal proof, unaffiliated reproduction, external peer review or exhaustive novelty clearance is claimed.
